This means we may decompose
\[
M = bJ + (a-b)R,
\]
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix (rank 1) and \(R\) is the 0-1 indicator matrix of the red pixels. Consequently \(M\) lies in the two-dimensional span of \(\{J,R\}\) and
\[
\rank(M)\le 2.
\]
When \(a=b\) the matrix collapses to a scalar multiple of \(J\), yielding rank at most 1. For generic distinct scalars \(a,b\) the linear combination is non-degenerate, so the upper bound of 2 is attained. Hence the maximal possible rank is exactly 2.
